ventures.title: Volatility-Adjusted Position-Sizing Spreadsheet for Retail Traders
ventures.thesis: Retail crypto/FX/equity traders routinely blow up accounts by sizing positions off gut feel instead of volatility. A ready-to-use spreadsheet that auto-computes position size from account equity, risk-per-trade %, and ATR-based stop distance is a proven, evergreen digital-product category (similar templates sell steadily on Gumroad/Etsy for $9-$29). Zero marginal cost, legal, no impersonation, pure genuine utility — I can fully draft the logic and layout now; a human just needs to build it in Sheets/Excel and list it.
ventures.deliverable:
SPREADSHEET SPEC + FORMULAS (ready to build in Google Sheets/Excel):

TAB 1: 'RiskCalc'
Columns: A=Asset, B=Account Equity ($), C=Risk % per trade (default 1%), D=Entry Price, E=Stop Price, F=Stop Distance = ABS(D-E), G=Risk $ = B*C, H=Position Size (units) = G/F, I=Position Notional ($) = H*D, J=Max Leverage Check = I/B (flag red if >5x via conditional formatting).

TAB 2: 'ATR Helper' — instructions for pulling 14-period ATR from TradingView/exchange and using ATR*multiplier (1.5-2x) as stop distance instead of a manual guess, with a worked example (BTC entry $86,000, ATR $1,800, stop = entry - 1.5*ATR = $83,300, on $10k account risking 1%, size = $100/$2,700 = 0.037 BTC = $3,182 notional).

TAB 3: 'Portfolio Heat' — sums risk $ across all open positions (pulls from Tab1 col G), flags if total open risk exceeds 6% of equity (conditional format red), enforcing a hard portfolio-level stop-loss discipline.

TAB 4: 'Trade Log' — Date, Asset, Direction, Entry, Exit, R-multiple realized (=(
 Exit-Entry)/Stop Distance), running equity curve chart.

Include a 1-page README explaining the 1%-risk rule, why volatility-based stops beat fixed %, and how to adapt multiplier by asset class (crypto 2x ATR, FX 1.5x ATR, equities 2x ATR).

ventures.title: Crypto DCA & Rebalance Planner (Google Sheets Template)
ventures.thesis: Retail crypto holders constantly ask 'how much should I buy/sell to get back to target weights' but don't want to build a spreadsheet. A clean, pre-built Google Sheets template that (a) tracks a target allocation across BTC/ETH/alts/stables, (b) computes drift vs targets, and (c) outputs exact buy/sell $ amounts to rebalance or to execute a scheduled DCA — sold once on Gumroad/Etsy for $9-15, zero marginal cost per sale, pure content/skill monetization, no ToS issues, no financial advice given (just arithmetic on user-entered numbers).
ventures.deliverable:
SHEET STRUCTURE (ready to build in Google Sheets, tabs and formulas specified):

TAB 1 'Setup': Columns A=Asset, B=Target Weight %, C=Current Holdings (units), D=Current Price (user pastes), E=Current Value =C*D, F=Total Portfolio Value =SUM(E), G=Current Weight % =E/F, H=Target Value =B*F, I=Drift $ =H-E, J=Action ('BUY'/'SELL'/'HOLD' via =IF(I>1,"BUY",IF(I<-1,"SELL","HOLD")), K=Amount to Trade $ =ABS(I).
Rows pre-filled for BTC, ETH, SOL, Stablecoin, 'Alts basket' — user edits freely, adds rows.

TAB 2 'DCA Schedule': Columns for Date, Planned Contribution $, Split % per asset (defaults to Target Weight from Tab1 via QUERY/VLOOKUP), computed $ per asset, running total invested, running total units bought (=Contribution*Split/Price entered that date) — gives a full DCA log the user fills in weekly/monthly.

TAB 3 'Dashboard': Pie chart of current vs target weights (native Sheets chart on Tab1 ranges), a single-cell total drift metric =SUMPRODUCT(ABS(I2:I10)) to show 'how far out of balance am I', and conditional formatting (red/green) on the Action column.

TAB 4 'Read Me': Plain-English instructions (no advice, just mechanics): how to fill in prices, how often to rebalance (e.g. monthly or >5% drift), disclaimer that this is a calculator not financial advice.

All formulas above are copy-paste-ready native Google Sheets syntax — this is a fully specified, buildable template, not just a concept.

ventures.title: Cross-Asset Weekly Brief — a Substack newsletter
ventures.thesis: I already synthesize crypto, FX, commodities and equities data every cycle. A concise weekly brief distilling correlations and regime shifts (e.g. 'BTC flat, DXY soft, gold near highs — what it means for risk assets') is a real, testable content product. Legal, no ToS conflict, distribution via Substack's free tier and organic sharing (Twitter/X, Reddit r/CryptoCurrency, r/algotrading). Monetizes via paid subscription tier once a free-issue track record exists.
ventures.deliverable:
DRAFT ISSUE #1 — 'Cross-Asset Weekly Brief, Sept 25 2026'

---
THIS WEEK IN ONE LINE: Crypto majors grinding sideways-up on light volume while gold and silver sit near record highs — a classic 'quiet before a macro print' setup.

1) CRYPTO: BTC $84,009 (+0.17% WoW), ETH $2,696 (+0.29%). Realized vol is compressing — BTC has moved <1% intraday for 5 straight sessions. Low vol regimes after a drawdown often resolve directionally within 1-2 weeks; watch $86k (recent local high) and $81k (recent local low) as the box to break.

2) GOLD & SILVER: PAXG $4,280, XAG $64.35 — both near cycle highs. This is the 'debasement trade': real yields soft, central banks still net buyers. If you're long crypto, gold is the natural hedge leg, not cash — it has held up better than BTC on every recent risk-off day this quarter.

3) FX: EURUSD 1.1399, GBPUSD 1.325, both flat. Dollar index sideways = no drag or tailwind on crypto risk this week. A break below 1.13 EURUSD would signal fresh dollar strength — historically a headwind for BTC in the following 5-10 days.

4) EQUITIES: SPY $770.91, QQQ $744.64 — mega-cap tech (NVDA, MSFT) drifting lower into month-end, small negative days stacking. Not a crash signal, just a pause after a strong run. Correlation between QQQ and BTC has been rising (both 'risk-on' proxies) — a real equity drawdown would likely drag crypto with it.

TAKEAWAY: Low-vol coiling in crypto + gold near highs + equities pausing = a market waiting for a catalyst (next CPI/FOMC). Reduce position sizing until range breaks; don't chase either direction inside the box.

---
(Format continues weekly, ~400-600 words, same five sections, free for first 4 issues to build an archive, then a paid tier at $5/mo for subscriber-only deeper dives.)

ventures.title: Pre-Launch Security & Ops Checklist for Small Solana/NFT Projects
ventures.thesis: Small token and NFT teams on Solana routinely skip basic pre-launch hygiene (wallet hygiene, multisig setup, metadata immutability checks, mint authority revocation, common drainer/phishing vectors) because a full paid audit is out of reach. A concise, honest checklist-and-review service (not a security 'certification') sold cheaply on Fiverr/Upwork fills that gap: I review their public contract/mint config and deployment plan against a structured checklist and return a marked-up PDF with concrete flagged risks. No code execution or guarantees claimed — explicitly framed as a hygiene review, not an audit, to stay honest and avoid overclaiming.
ventures.deliverable:
CHECKLIST v1 (delivered as the actual gig output):
1. MINT AUTHORITY: Is mint authority revoked/renounced post-supply-lock? (check via explorer)
2. FREEZE AUTHORITY: Is freeze authority null unless intentionally used (e.g. compliance token)?
3. METADATA: Is metadata URI pinned (IPFS/Arweave) not a mutable centralized URL? Is update authority a multisig or burned?
4. LP LOCK: If launching liquidity, is LP locked/burned with a verifiable lock contract and duration stated publicly?
5. TEAM WALLET TRANSPARENCY: Are team/treasury wallets disclosed and vesting terms public?
6. SOCIAL SURFACE: Are official Discord/Twitter/Telegram links consistent everywhere, with no unofficial mod DM policy stated (anti-phishing)?
7. SITE/DAPP: Does the connect-wallet flow request only expected permissions (no blanket approve-all)? Is the domain the one publicized on all official channels (typosquat check)?
8. MULTISIG: Are upgrade/admin keys on a Squads or equivalent multisig, not a single EOA?
9. RUGCHECK CROSS-REF: Cross-reference against a public rugcheck-style tool output and reconcile discrepancies.
10. COMMUNICATION HONESTY: No promised APY/returns claims on marketing copy without disclosed source of yield.
Delivered as: 1-page PDF scorecard (pass/flag/fail per item) + 3-5 bullet written risk summary. Explicitly labeled 'hygiene checklist review, not a security audit or guarantee.'

ventures.killCriteria: If no orders within 30 days of publishing, or if any client expects an actual smart-contract code audit (scope mismatch), kill and redirect effort to a narrower checklist-only product.
